data.title: Week Without Waste
data.summary:
Take the Week Without Waste Challenge! Can you fit all your landfill waste into a Mason jar? Reduce, reuse, recycle, and rethink your habits—let’s see how small you can shrink your waste this week!

Learn more and collect your Mason jar (or use your own!) from our office (Pavilion Suite 229) or from our team on April 1, 2026, 11 a.m.–2 p.m., Memorial Student Center, at the Office of Sustainability & Campus Enrichment table!

Document your participation in Week Without Waste by filling out this short form and earn up to 20 entries into our Earth Month Grand Prize Drawings. Submissions are due by April 11, 2026. Points can be earned as follows:

  • Photo of your jar (or you & your jar) at the end of the week (5 points)
  • Reflection (5 points)
  • Additional photos (2points/unique photo MAX 10 - validity determined by OSCE Staff).
To learn more about Campus Earth Month and our grand prize giveaway, see this link.

data.title: Is Clean Energy Actually Clean?
data.summary: We’re told that the future is clean energy, but what actually goes into it? In our talk, we dive into the world of energy transition minerals. Join us as we explore the complex trade-offs between global sustainability goals and the environmental realities of the mines that make them possible. From policy shifts to community impacts, we’re questioning if a truly clean future exists and what it will take to get there.

data.title: Caring for What Can’t Speak for Itself: Rights for Animals and Plants for Future Generations
data.summary: This talk examines our role as humans in environmental stewardship, the moral consideration we give to the interests of plants, animals, and future generations, all of which are unable to communicate their needs and interests to us. We argue that plants and animals have intrinsic value, or value within themselves, and that future generations deserve to see the beauty and aesthetics of the planet just as we have. This is based on the belief that all plants and animals have an interest in living, therefore worthy of our consideration in otherwise anthropocentric developments. By rethinking our role in environmental stewardship, we can begin making choices today that protect the world we leave behind.

data.title: Biomimicry: Nature as Our Mentor
data.summary: In this TED Talk, we will dive into the science behind biomimicry, case studies of sustainable innovations that emulate natural models, and how it can benefit the circular economy. Ultimately, we will explore how shifting our perspective from learning about nature to learning from nature offers a blueprint for healing our planet

data.title: Campus Earth Day
data.summary: Join the Office of Sustainability & Campus Enrichment and other university and community partners as we share how to make Aggieland greener. Earth Day celebrations include games and the opportunity to win prizes and a free T-shirt.
data.description:
This year’s event will feature pictures with Reveille from 11–11:30 a.m. All attendees can earn a FREE Sustainability shirt for participating!

You can earn additional entries into our Earth Month giveaway by visiting our partner tables. Visit TX.AG/EarthMonth for a full list of our events, our giveaway prizes, and other opportunities to participate!

Earth Day is a feature event of our Campus Earth Month festivities, which serve as an arena for sustainability awareness and education. We want everyone to be effective leaders in their environment, whether that is A&M, Bryan, College Station, or at home. Our goal is to expose, educate, and empower attendees with the skills they need to be more sustainable - environmentally, socially, and economically.

data.title: Hullabloom Fest - The Gardens
data.summary: Celebrate the magic of spring — and the pollinators who make it possible — at The Gardens Hullabloom Fest! This joyful community event invites guests of all ages to explore the vibrant world of bees, butterflies, and other garden helpers through hands‑on activities, educational stations, and blooming seasonal displays.
data.description:
Enjoy light refreshments, educational demonstrations, gardening resources, and family‑friendly crafts inspired by wings, petals, and everything in between. And of course we hope you’ll take part in what has become the highlight of the Hullabloom Fest: the butterfly release.

We will have a Sensory Free/Quiet Zone during the Hullabloom Fest for anyone who may want or need a quieter environment at any point during the event.

This event is a free event that is open to the community.

Schedule of Events

9:00 AM – Event Begins
Wander through The Gardens, visit table partners, grab a refreshment, and don’t forget to sign up to release a butterfly.
11:00 AM – Butterfly Release
We will begin handing out butterflies to those who signed up to release one at 10:45 am. Once all butterflies are handed out, we will gather and release on The Event Lawn.
11:30 AM – Event Ends
Thanks for joining us!

Unable to join us? No worries!

Here are a few ways you can still enjoy Spring out in The Gardens!

  • Download our scavenger hunt and explore The Gardens as you race to see who can find all of the items first!
  • Bring your camera for photos in front of our spring blooms wall at any time this April!
  • Create and enjoy one of these delicious spring recipes from Texas A&M AgriLife Extension Service’s Dinner Tonight program.
    • Quick Chicken & Spring Vegetables
    • Peach & Blackberry Salad
    • Homemade Basil Pesto

Parking Information

Attendees can park for free in Lots 97 or 100c. More information about our parking options can be found at Parking and Transportation.

data.title: Internship Applications Close
data.summary: The Office of Sustainability & Campus Enrichment’s Undergraduate Internship Program applications open today. Learn more at sustainability.tamu.edu.
data.description:
The goal of the Office of Sustainability & Campus Enrichment’s Internship Program is to bring undergraduate students from a variety of backgrounds and perspectives together to create a dynamic team that works to create a culture of sustainability at Texas A&M University. Interns work together to increase awareness and education about the three pillars of sustainability: environmental, economic, and social. The team focuses on educating the campus community about topics such as: energy and water use, transportation, food services, construction and built environment, purchasing, recycling, and social sustainability through the development of outreach initiatives and event coordination. Additionally, interns support assessment and planning efforts prioritized by the office.

The Internship Program is open to any TAMU undergraduate student and all majors are encouraged to apply because true sustainability must be an interdisciplinary enterprise.

Applications are open March 17th, 2026 – April 19th, 2026 at sustainability.tamu.edu.
